$comment: Editorial descriptions of works, merged into each work's manifest at sync time by
scripts/sync-corpus.mjs and rendered by /documenta (and anywhere else reading
`manifest.description`).
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS RATHER THAN A FIELD IN the corpus's works/*/manifest.json: those
manifests are GENERATED. A re-parse rewrites them, so a description written there
survives exactly until the next parser fix — and this project fixes parsers by
re-parsing (CLAUDE.md's 're-parse, never re-crawl'). Descriptions are editorial, not
scraped, so they live in tracked source and are merged in on the way to the site. The
corpus stays purely generated and re-parsing stays free of consequences. Same posture,
same reasoning, and the same place as unpublished.json.
SHAPE: work id -> language -> { text, origin }. The outer key is the work being
described, so the two language editions of one document are described separately — a
description read from the Portuguese edition is prose about THAT text, not a translated
label. The inner key is the language the prose is written in, which is the work's own
language for a reading and any UI language for a translation of one.
ORIGIN IS THE WHOLE POINT OF THE SHAPE, and the two values are not interchangeable:
"read"       — written by READING THE DOCUMENT IN THE CORPUS. The rule in
docs/writing-descriptions.md is not negotiable: never from recollection
of what a document with that title probably says. A plausible-sounding
wrong description is worse than none, because nothing on the rendered
page distinguishes it from a real summary.
"translated" — derived from another rendering of the SAME work, named in `from`.
A translation is never written from the document; it inherits whatever
the reading got right and whatever it got wrong, which is exactly why
it is labelled rather than merged into the same field. `from` makes the
provenance a chain that can be checked: correct a reading and every
translation of it is known to be stale.
A work with no entry simply has no description; nothing renders a placeholder.

en.text: Pius X's encyclical on the neglect of religious instruction, arguing that widespread ignorance of Christian doctrine — even among the educated — is the root of moral decline, and that teaching it is a pastor's first duty under the Council of Trent. It closes with six binding ordinances: weekly catechism for children, First Communion preparation, a parish Confraternity of Christian Doctrine, and adult instruction on holy days.

Benedict XV's first encyclical, issued three months into the First World War, appeals for an end to the fighting and traces its underlying causes to a decline in mutual charity, contempt for authority, and class conflict between rich and poor, naming love of money as their deepest root. It also calls on Catholics to abandon factional labels and remain united with their bishops, then closes with a prayer for peace.

Pius X marks the golden jubilee of the definition of the Immaculate Conception, urging renewed devotion to Mary as the surest way of restoring all things in Christ. He sets out her singular part in the work of redemption and her office as mediatrix of grace, calls the faithful to imitate her faith, hope and charity, and closes by proclaiming a jubilee indulgence with its conditions.

John XXIII's first encyclical, written at the start of his pontificate around the recognition of truth, “a renewal of Christian morals,” and “a restoration of unity, harmony, and peace.” It addresses truth against error and the press's duties, unity among nations, within the family, and within the Church around the newly announced Ecumenical Council, then counsels bishops, clergy, religious, and the sick.

pt.text: Primeira carta encíclica de João XXIII, dirigida a todo o orbe católico, sobre o conhecimento da verdade, a restauração da unidade e da paz na caridade. Trata da verdade e do indiferentismo religioso, da concórdia entre povos, classes e famílias, da unidade da Igreja em torno da Cátedra de Pedro, e encerra com exortações paternais a bispos, clero, religiosos, missionários, pobres, refugiados e à Igreja perseguida.

en.text: Leo XIII's encyclical urging Catholics to devote the month of October to the Rosary, presenting it as the most effective prayer for the object then closest to his heart: the reconciliation of nations separated from the Church, above all in the Christian East. He recounts Mary's historic role as guardian of Church unity, from Dominic Guzman's preaching to earlier popes' efforts to spread the devotion in the East.

pt.text: Carta encíclica de Leão XIII sobre o Rosário como via de retorno à unidade da Igreja. Pede orações perseverantes pela reconciliação dos povos separados do Oriente e do Ocidente, apresenta Maria — evocando o Concílio de Éfeso — como o vínculo capaz de reuni-los sob o Pontífice Romano, e anuncia a construção de um templo à Rainha do Rosário em Patras.

en.text: John XXIII's encyclical for the fifteenth centenary of the death of Pope St. Leo the Great, recounting Leo's life, his defense of the faith against the Nestorian and Pelagian heresies, and his teaching on the primacy of the Roman See as the center of the Church's visible unity. With the Second Vatican Council approaching, it turns that example into a renewed call for unity among all Christians.

On the restoration of Christian philosophy, and specifically of St Thomas Aquinas, in Catholic schools. Leo XIII sets out philosophy's proper office as handmaid to faith, surveys what the Fathers and the Scholastics made of it, singles out Thomas as the master whose method keeps faith and reason each in its right, and directs bishops to make his doctrine the foundation of clerical and university teaching.

Benedict XV renews, for a second Christmas, his appeal on behalf of the starving and disease-stricken children of Central Europe left destitute by the war. He asks that a collection be taken up on the feast of the Holy Innocents, or the preceding Sunday, for their relief, to be forwarded to him or to the Save the Children Fund, and pledges one hundred thousand lire of his own.

Leo XIII's encyclical on Christian marriage: Christ raised it to a sacrament and restored the unity and indissolubility it had lost, so the Church holds authority over the marriages of the baptized. It argues against treating marriage as a merely civil contract subject to the state, sets out the evils that follow from divorce, and closes commending to the bishops those living outside a lawful bond.

Leo XIII's encyclical on the Confraternity of the Holy Rosary, written in his eighty-eighth year and framed as a dying father's repetition of Christ's “Behold, thy Mother.” It argues that the age's appetite for association is good in itself, that Catholics should meet it with sodalities rather than abandon it, and that the Rosary Society is the first of them — defending prayer to the saints as intercession rather than as a rival to prayer to God.

On integral human development in charity and truth, taking up Paul VI's Populorum Progressio forty years on. Charity in truth is set out as the principle of the Church's social doctrine and then applied: to the global financial crisis, to the ethics of business and the market, to gratuitousness and gift, to the environment, to cooperation between peoples, and to the human meaning of technology and bioethics.

Pius XI's encyclical on Christian marriage, organized around St. Augustine's three blessings of wedlock — offspring, conjugal faith, and the sacrament — expounding each in turn before cataloguing the errors attacking them: contraception, abortion, eugenic sterilization, divorce, and the “false emancipation” of women, and closing with remedies for restoring marriage to the divine plan.

Paul VI asks the whole Church to pray the Rosary through October 1966 for peace, with war in eastern Asia and a nuclear arms race in view, invoking Mary as Queen of Peace. He presses the nations toward sincere negotiation, asks that 4 October — the anniversary of his appeal at the United Nations — be kept as a day of prayer, and closes with a Marian appeal for justice and a lasting peace.

An appeal for the month of May 1945, three weeks before the war in Europe ended: Pius XII asks the faithful, and children in particular, to pray to Mary for peace and for the renewal of Christian morals on which peace rests, and to pray for refugees, prisoners and the wounded — so that what follows the devastation may be a just peace and not one carrying the seed of future wars.

Pius X marks the eighth centenary of the death of St. Anselm of Canterbury, praising his sanctity and his stand for the Church's liberty against secular encroachment, then holds him up as founder of a scholastic middle way between rationalist excess and fideist neglect — deployed as a direct warning against modernist "agnosticism" and dialecticians who overreach reason's limits.

Leo XIII's encyclical to the bishops and clergy of France on forming priests. It sets a curriculum: classical letters for junior seminaries, then rational philosophy grounded in Aeterni Patris against modern errors, scholastic theology built on St. Thomas's Summa, the Roman Catechism, Scripture, Church history and canon law for senior ones — then turns to ordained priests, urging obedience to their bishops and zeal tempered by prudence.

On the meaning of Christian love: it follows eros and agape from their ancient distinction to their unity in biblical revelation and the Incarnation, then turns to the Church's charitable activity — alongside proclaiming the word and celebrating the sacraments — as belonging to her own nature, its relation to justice and its organisation, closing with the saints and Mary as the exemplars of charity.

pt.text: Trata do amor cristão a partir de « Deus é amor » (1 Jo 4, 16): a primeira parte busca a unidade entre eros e agape na criação e na história da salvação, culminando no amor a Deus e ao próximo revelados em Jesus Cristo; a segunda volta-se para a caritas como prática da Igreja enquanto « comunidade de amor », discutindo justiça, caridade e seus responsáveis.

en.text: Francis's 2024 encyclical on devotion to the Sacred Heart of Jesus: what the symbol of the 'heart' can still mean for a distracted age, what Christ's own gaze, words and pierced side reveal about his human and divine love, the history of this devotion from Margaret Mary through Francis de Sales, Claude de la Colombière, Charles de Foucauld and Thérèse of Lisieux, and how reparation for love unreturned extends into fraternity, mission and social concern.

On the origin of civil power, written after a run of attacks on the lives of European rulers. Leo XIII rejects the doctrine that authority is merely delegated by popular will, traces the ruler's power to God through Scripture and the Fathers, bounds obedience by the higher duty to divine and natural law, recalls the Church's deference toward pagan and Christian rulers alike, and asks bishops to preach this against sedition.

On the mercy of God, revealed above all in Christ crucified and risen and read through the parable of the prodigal son. It follows mercy from the covenant with Israel to the Paschal Mystery, weighs it against the anxieties of the modern world and against the demand for justice alone, and closes asking the Church to proclaim mercy, to practise it, and to beg for it from generation to generation.

Pius XI's encyclical on atheistic communism, written as its persecution intensified in Russia, Mexico and Spain. It traces communism's Marxist materialism, how it strips man of liberty and dignity and would dissolve family and property into a collectivity built for production, opposes to it the Church's teaching on God, man and society, and prescribes remedies — renewed Christian life, social justice, Catholic Action — under St. Joseph's protection.

pt.text: Carta encíclica de Pio XI sobre o comunismo ateu, escrita quando a sua perseguição já lavrava na Rússia, no México e na Espanha. Expõe a doutrina comunista e o seu materialismo marxista, com frutos deploráveis como a luta contra tudo o que se chama Deus e o terrorismo, opondo-lhe a doutrina católica sobre Deus, o homem e a sociedade, e indicando remédios: renovação da vida cristã, justiça social e Ação Católica.

en.text: On biblical studies, fifty years after Leo XIII's Providentissimus Deus. Pius XII directs Catholic exegetes to work from the original Hebrew, Greek and Aramaic rather than from the Vulgate alone, to use textual criticism, and to identify the literary genres of the ancient Near East before judging what a passage means — closing with an appeal that priests draw their preaching and their own spiritual life from Scripture.

On the Holy Spirit, completing the Trinitarian sequence begun with Redemptor Hominis on the Son and Dives in Misericordia on the Father. In three parts it follows the Spirit given at the Supper and at Pentecost, his work of convincing the world concerning sin — including the sin against the Holy Spirit — and his office as the giver of life, with the Jubilee of the third millennium in view.

Pius X's inaugural encyclical, taking the Apostle's phrase "to restore all things in Christ" as the whole programme of his pontificate. He reads his age's apostasy from God as a deep-rooted disease, makes the Church the way back to Christ, and asks bishops for holy priests, well-governed seminaries, patient religious instruction, and charity rather than bitterness toward those estranged.

it.text: Nel terzo centenario del martirio di san Giosafat, arcivescovo di Polock, l'enciclica ripercorre lo scisma bizantino degli Slavi orientali e l'unione di Brest del 1596, poi la vita di Giosafat, monaco basiliano e vescovo, ucciso nel 1623 per la causa dell'unità. Pio XI lo propone come patrono dei cattolici e dei dissidenti orientali, invitandoli alla preghiera e alla reciproca conoscenza in vista del ritorno alla piena comunione con la Sede Apostolica.

en.text: Paul VI's first encyclical, written one year into his pontificate as a statement of governing priorities: the Church's need for deeper self-awareness, the renewal called for by the Second Vatican Council, and dialogue with the world. The final and longest part elaborates dialogue as method, extending it outward through concentric circles — from all mankind, to believers in one God, to other Christians, to Catholics themselves.

Marking the third centenary of St. Charles Borromeo's canonization, Pius X holds him up as the model of true reform: fidelity to Rome and self-effacing zeal against heresy, opposed both to the Protestant revolt Borromeo fought and to what Pius calls the apostasy of his own day. It contrasts the true reformer, who trusts God and the Church, with the false one, who seeks his own glory, closing with an appeal to Catholic Action.

Leo XIII's encyclical to the bishops of Italy, confronting a “pernicious sect” exploiting the country's altered political condition to strip away its Christian institutions. Recalling Italy's historic debts to the papacy, it charges the bishops to rouse Catholic courage through associations, a sound press against hostile journalism, and rigorously formed seminaries, closing with an appeal to Mary and the saints.

pt.text: Sobre o valor da vida humana e a sua inviolabilidade, diante das novas ameaças do aborto e da eutanásia: parte do grito do sangue de Abel e do eclipse do sentido da vida, percorre o mandamento «não matarás» perante a lei civil e a lei moral, e chama a uma nova cultura da vida, terminando com uma prece a Maria, Mãe dos viventes.

en.text: On fraternity and social friendship, opening from St Francis of Assisi's love that crossed every border. It surveys a closed and throwaway world of nationalism and fear, reads the Good Samaritan as the call to an open society built on solidarity and the rights of peoples, and argues for a political charity against populism, for dialogue and forgiveness after conflict, against war and the death penalty, and for fraternity between religions.

pt.text: Carta encíclica de Francisco sobre a fraternidade e a amizade social, inspirada no apelo de São Francisco de Assis, de quem toma o título. Parte da parábola do bom samaritano para denunciar as sombras dum mundo fechado e propor a política melhor, o diálogo e a amizade social, e o papel das religiões ao serviço da fraternidade no mundo.

en.text: An account of Sts Cyril and Methodius, the ninth-century brothers sent from Constantinople to the Slavs of Moravia: their formation, their commission from Rome, the charge that a liturgy in the Slavonic tongue broke with Church custom — answered and allowed in Rome — and their deaths. Leo XIII extends their feast to the universal Church on 5 July and asks their intercession for reconciliation with the East.

John XXIII on the October Rosary, recalling that Leo XIII and Pius XII had made the same appeal before him. He asks prayers for the missionaries about to leave for the foreign missions and for the centenary of the North American College, for rulers weighing the causes of international discord, against the errors of laicism and materialism, and for the coming Roman Synod and Ecumenical Council.

Pius X's follow-up to Vehementer Nos, addressed to the French bishops after the 1905 separation law. It rules that the associations of worship the law requires cannot be formed without violating the Church's divine constitution and the rights of pope and bishops over ecclesiastical property, and directs the bishops instead to organize worship through whatever lawful means remain open to them.

Pius XII's encyclical on devotion to the Sacred Heart of Jesus, issued for the centenary of the feast's institution. It grounds the devotion in Scripture and the Fathers, argues that the Heart symbolizes Christ's threefold love — divine, spiritual and human — shown in the Eucharist, in Mary and in the Church, and exhorts the faithful to renewed practice through love, reparation and consecration.

pt.text: Carta encíclica de Pio XII sobre o culto ao Sagrado Coração de Jesus, escrita para o centenário da instituição da festa por Pio IX. Percorre os fundamentos desse culto nas Escrituras do Antigo e do Novo Testamento, na tradição dos Padres e no seu desenvolvimento histórico até à Idade Média, e conclui exortando os fiéis a praticá-lo com maior fervor.

en.text: Paul VI on the regulation of birth, in three parts: the Church's competence to interpret the natural moral law, the doctrinal principles, and pastoral directives. It rests on an inseparable connection between the unitive and procreative meanings of the marriage act, excluding abortion, sterilisation and contraception while permitting recourse to infertile periods, and asks scientists for a more secure knowledge of natural rhythms.

pt.text: Carta encíclica de Paulo VI sobre a regulação da natalidade. Reafirma a ligação inseparável entre união e procriação no ato conjugal, defende a paternidade responsável e exclui como ilícitos o aborto, a esterilização direta e os métodos artificiais de contracepção, admitindo apenas o recurso aos períodos infecundos. Termina com apelos aos governantes, cientistas, esposos, médicos, sacerdotes e bispos.

en.text: Benedict XV on preaching: never have there been more preachers, he observes, and never has the harvest been thinner. He blames men who run unsent, preach themselves and hunt applause, asks bishops to weigh character and learning before granting faculties as strictly as for confessors, and holds up St Paul — conformed to God's will, a man of prayer, preaching Christ crucified — as the measure.

Leo XIII's encyclical on Freemasonry, framing history as a struggle between two opposed kingdoms and naming Freemasonry as the organizing centre of a wider network of secret societies. It traces their doctrine to naturalism and the denial of revelation, which it holds corrodes marriage, education and civil authority, and prescribes religious instruction, the revival of workers' guilds, and the Third Order of St. Francis.

pt.text: Carta encíclica de Leão XIII sobre a Maçonaria, que apresenta a história como luta entre duas cidades opostas — a terrena e a celestial — e identifica a seita dos maçons como centro de uma rede de sociedades secretas. Atribui a sua doutrina ao naturalismo, que corrompe o casamento, a educação e a autoridade civil, e propõe remédios: instrução religiosa, associações de trabalhadores e a Ordem Terceira de São Francisco.

en.text: Written to the Italian bishops to organise the lay Catholic works — what came to be called Catholic Action — under the single aim of restoring all things in Christ. Pius X defines the movement's scope, ties its social work to Rerum Novarum, prescribes a Popular Union to hold it together, repeats the ban on direct participation in politics, and subordinates every such work to the bishops.

Leo XIII's encyclical on the Christian constitution of states: civil authority comes from God, not from the sovereignty of the people, and is bound to honor religion publicly. Rejecting the naturalist doctrines that exclude God from public life, it sets out the concord due between Church and State, and closes urging Catholics to take an active part in public affairs despite lawful disagreement over forms of government.

pt.text: Carta encíclica de Leão XIII sobre a constituição cristã dos Estados: defende que o poder público só pode vir de Deus, expõe a Igreja como sociedade perfeita e soberana na sua esfera própria, distinta mas harmónica com o poder civil, refuta a tese liberal de separar os negócios da Igreja dos do Estado, e conclui exortando os católicos à unidade na participação da vida política.

en.text: For the twelfth centenary of St Boniface's mission to Germany, written to the German hierarchy amid the disorder that followed the First World War. Benedict XV retraces Boniface's oath of fidelity to the Holy See, his correspondence with successive popes and his martyrdom, holds them up as the pattern of Germany's ancient union with Rome, urges its restoration, and grants indulgences for the centenary.

Pius XI's encyclical on the persecution of the Catholic Church in Mexico under the 1917 Constitution and its 1926 enforcement laws, which stripped the Church of civil status, barred clergy from teaching, expelled foreign priests and religious, and closed schools and seminaries. He reviews the resistance of Mexico's bishops, clergy, and lay organizations, and commends the country to Our Lady of Guadalupe.

Leo XIII's first encyclical, written days into his pontificate: a survey of the evils he sees oppressing society — the subversion of first truths, contempt for lawful authority, family life corrupted — traced to the setting aside of the Church's authority, and answered by recalling what the papacy has done for civilization and by pressing bishops toward a Christian education of youth begun at home.

Written for the thirteenth centenary of the death of St Gregory the Great, holding up his pastoral government — restoring faith and discipline while Rome collapsed around him — as the pattern for an age in crisis of unbelief. Pius X traces how rationalism and a misapplied critical science wear faith away, insists that only a return to Christ can save society, and asks for careful formation of candidates for the priesthood.

On human work as a fundamental dimension of man's existence, ninety years after Rerum Novarum. It separates work's objective sense — technology, the thing made — from its subjective sense, the person working, argues from that the priority of labour over capital, sets out the rights it founds in wages, unions, disabled and migrant workers, and closes on a spirituality of work drawn from Genesis and from Christ, himself a man of work.

Francis's encyclical on ecology, taking its title from Saint Francis's Canticle of the Creatures. It diagnoses pollution, climate change, water scarcity, biodiversity loss and social breakdown as symptoms of one crisis rooted in a 'technocratic paradigm,' develops an 'integral ecology' linking care for nature to justice for the poor, and proposes lines of dialogue, education, and 'ecological conversion.'

pt.text: Carta encíclica de Francisco, dirigida a cada pessoa que habita este planeta, sobre o cuidado da casa comum. Parte do diagnóstico do que está a acontecer à Terra — poluição, mudanças climáticas, perda de biodiversidade, desigualdade — para propor uma ecologia integral que una a questão ambiental à justiça social, recusando o paradigma tecnocrático e convidando à conversão ecológica; termina com duas orações.

en.text: Leo XIII's encyclical on the nature of human liberty, arguing true freedom lies in the will's conformity to the eternal law of God, not in acting simply as one pleases. It examines and limits the liberties liberalism champions — of worship, of speech and the press, of teaching, and of conscience — rejects unconditional separation of Church and State, and allows that Catholics may licitly prefer democratic government.

Leo XIII's encyclical to the Belgian bishops on preserving Catholic unity amid disputes over how far Catholic doctrine should govern the forms of civil law and government. He urges charity in controversy, rebukes attacks on fellow Catholics — naming the accusations against Cardinal Deschamps — and directs scholars to follow St. Thomas Aquinas as the model for philosophy and theology, renewing his call for Thomistic teaching at Louvain.

On faith as the light of Christ by which human life is guided — the encyclical that completes the trilogy on the theological virtues, drafted by Benedict XVI before his resignation and finished by Francis. It follows faith from Abraham and Israel to Christ, examines its bond with truth and with reason, its transmission through the Church's creed and sacraments, and its power to sustain the family, society and those who suffer.

Leo XIV's encyclical on artificial intelligence and the social doctrine of the Church. Framed by two biblical images of collective building — the Tower of Babel and Nehemiah's rebuilding of Jerusalem — it argues that AI is not one more subject for social doctrine to address but a development that challenges its categories from within, and takes up human dignity and the common good, truth, work and freedom, and the growing place of autonomous systems in war.

pt.text: Carta encíclica de Leão XIV sobre a inteligência artificial e a doutrina social da Igreja. Estruturada em torno de duas imagens bíblicas da construção comum — a Torre de Babel e a reconstrução de Jerusalém por Neemias —, sustenta que a IA não é mais um tema a tratar pela doutrina social, mas um desenvolvimento que desafia as suas próprias categorias, e aborda a dignidade humana e o bem comum, a verdade, o trabalho e a liberdade, e o lugar crescente dos sistemas autónomos na guerra.

en.text: John XXIII's restatement of Catholic social teaching on the seventieth anniversary of Rerum Novarum, carrying Leo XIII's principles forward through Quadragesimo Anno and Pius XII's radio addresses. It then takes up newer aspects of the social question — the depressed state of agriculture, the gap between developed and developing nations, population growth, and international cooperation — and closes with principles for rebuilding a social order on truth, justice, and love.

Settles the question of the Diocesan Associations, left open in France since the separation law of 1905. Reviewing the associations cultuelles that Pius X had condemned, Pius XI approves new statutes negotiated with the French government and examined by canonists and the Council of State, permits the dioceses to form associations under them, and repeats his predecessor's condemnation of the Lay Laws.

The sacred liturgy as the public worship that the Church, united with Christ her divine Head, offers to God: the priesthood's role in the Eucharistic sacrifice, the laity's active yet real participation in it, the sacraments and sacramentals, the Divine Office and liturgical year, and pastoral counsel on sacred art, music and altar servers, warning against both careless innovation and an exaggerated antiquarian zeal for reviving ancient forms.

Paul VI asks that the month of May be given to prayer to Mary for two urgent reasons: the Second Vatican Council, still sitting, and a peace in jeopardy as international tensions worsen. He condemns the disregard for human life that armed conflict brings, appeals to the world's rulers to renounce force, and asks children and the suffering in particular to pray the Rosary for peace.

pt.text: Carta encíclica de Pio XI aos bispos católicos sobre a unidade verdadeira da religião, contra o movimento "pancristão" e seus congressos ecumênicos, que buscam uma fraternidade comum ignorando as diferenças doutrinárias. Pio XI ensina que só existe uma religião verdadeira, revelada por Deus e guardada pela Igreja Católica, e que a unidade dos cristãos só se dá pelo retorno dos dissidentes a essa única Igreja, em obediência ao Romano Pontífice.

en.text: Mysterium Fidei, on the Holy Eucharist, written while the Council was still sitting to check opinions then circulating that would reduce the Real Presence to symbolism or put transignification in the place of transubstantiation. It reaffirms the Mass as both sacrifice and sacrament, defends Trent's language on Christ's substantial presence and the adoration due the Sacrament, and closes urging daily Mass and Eucharistic devotion.

On the Church as the Mystical Body of Christ: a single visible Body with Christ as Head, animated by the Holy Spirit and built up through the sacraments and the juridical bonds of faith, hope and charity. It refutes rationalist, naturalist and mystical errors about the Church's nature and closes by entrusting her peace to the Virgin Mary.

pt.text: Sobre o Corpo Místico de Cristo, que é a Igreja: define-a como um corpo único, visível e organicamente estruturado, cuja cabeça é Cristo e cujo vigário visível é o Papa, vivificada interiormente pelo Espírito Santo e unida pelos sacramentos, sobretudo a Eucaristia. Denuncia os erros do falso misticismo e do quietismo, exorta à caridade ativa para com a Igreja e encerra confiando os fiéis à Virgem Maria.

en.text: Pius XII's encyclical marking the 350th anniversary of the Union of Brest, by which the Ruthenian Church entered communion with Rome. It traces that reunion's history — the negotiations of 1595–96, the martyrdom of Josaphat Kuntsevych, and Rome's steady defense of the Ruthenian rite against Latinization — before turning to the persecution then engulfing the Ruthenian Church and exhorting its bishops, priests, and faithful to constancy.

For the fifteenth centenary of St Cyril of Alexandria, recounting his defence of the unity of Christ's person against Nestorius, his deference to the Apostolic See through the Council of Ephesus, and his patient reconciliation with the Antiochene bishops — which Pius XII holds up as the model for reunion with the separated Christians of the East, the modern Nestorians and those who do not receive Chalcedon.

On charity and mutual pardon between men and between nations, written weeks after the peace treaties that ended the First World War. Benedict XV presses for the forgiving of wartime enmities, commends practical relief for the widows, the orphans and the devastated regions, and calls the states to unite in a league — a family of peoples — to reduce armaments and keep the peace.

John XXIII's call to the whole Church, clergy and laity alike, for prayer and penance in preparation for the Second Vatican Council, invoking Scripture's repeated calls to penance and the precedent of earlier councils. It urges a solemn novena to the Holy Spirit carrying a plenary indulgence, and distinguishes internal repentance — confession and the Eucharist — from the voluntary external acts of penance offered for the Council's success.

Pius X's systematic condemnation of Modernism as “the synthesis of all heresies,” set out through the several roles a Modernist combines — philosopher, believer, theologian, historian and critic, apologist, reformer — and tracing agnosticism and “vital immanence” through his account of dogma, Scripture, and the Church. It then prescribes remedies: scholastic philosophy in seminaries, censorship of publications, and diocesan vigilance councils reporting to Rome every three years.

An appeal for the starving and destitute children of central Europe after the First World War. Benedict XV commends the Save the Children societies formed to help them, directs bishops to order public prayers and to gather alms, food, medicine and clothing on the feast of the Holy Innocents, and pledges a hundred thousand lire of his own toward the relief.

Pius X's admonition to the Italian bishops against a spirit of insubordination and independence spreading among the younger clergy. It demands strict seminary discipline, regulates who may preach and publish, reaffirms earlier norms governing “Popular Christian Action”, and forbids clerics from joining any society lacking episcopal approval, naming the National Democratic League specifically.

Paul VI's encyclical on the development of peoples, arguing that authentic development must be integral — of the whole man and of every man — and tracing the passage from less than human to more human conditions. It sets out the wealthier nations' threefold duty toward developing ones — solidarity, social justice and universal charity — and closes on development as the new name for peace.

pt.text: Carta encíclica de Paulo VI sobre o desenvolvimento dos povos, defendendo um desenvolvimento integral — do homem todo e de todos os homens — e a passagem de condições menos humanas, marcadas pela miséria e pela opressão, a condições mais humanas. Aponta o tríplice dever das nações ricas para com as mais pobres — solidariedade, justiça social e caridade universal — e conclui que o desenvolvimento é o novo nome da paz.

en.text: Princeps Pastorum, on the missions forty years after Benedict XV's Maximum Illud. John XXIII treats the formation of a native clergy — local hierarchies, seminaries that form men in holiness, a missiology fitted to the mind of each people while guarding unity against ultranationalism — then the apostolate of the laity through Catholic Action, catechists and the Christian school, closing with an appeal for vocations and for perseverance under persecution.

Benedict XV's encyclical proclaiming St. Ephrem the Syrian, deacon of Edessa, a Doctor of the Universal Church, with his feast fixed on 18 June. A companion to his encyclical on St. Jerome, it recounts Ephrem's life, teaching and hymnody — “the lyre of the Holy Spirit” — his devotion to the Virgin and to Peter's primacy, and appeals for the reunion of the separated Eastern churches with Rome.

Pius XI's encyclical for the fortieth anniversary of Leo XIII's On the Condition of Workers, treated under three headings: that encyclical's fruits, Catholic teaching on property's individual and social character and on just wages, and a verdict on the present economic order — wealth concentrated into an “economic dictatorship,” free competition's self-destruction, and Socialism's irreconcilability with Christianity — closing with a call to restore society through vocational guilds and reform of morals.

On the kingship of Christ over persons, families and states, gathering the scriptural, patristic and liturgical evidence for a dominion the age's anticlericalism had set out to deny. Closing the Holy Year of 1925, it institutes the feast of Christ the King on the last Sunday of October and joins to it the yearly renewal of the consecration of mankind to the Sacred Heart.

Pius XII's post-war appeal to the bishops on behalf of the world's destitute children, millions of whom the conflict left without food, shelter, clothing, or care. He asks that a day of public prayer be set aside in every diocese and urges the faithful to support relief through prayer, almsgiving, and organized charitable works, warning that neglect now will breed sickness, vice, and delinquency in the next generation.

On socialism, communism and nihilism, whose rise Leo XIII traces to the sixteenth-century revolt against the Catholic faith and to the philosophers' doctrine of unbridled liberty. It defends legitimate civil authority, the indissolubility of marriage and the family, and the natural right of private property against claims of absolute equality and common ownership, and asks bishops to keep workingmen out of the sect.

Written three weeks after the Armistice, with the peace congress about to meet: Benedict XV asks the bishops to order public prayers in every parish for its success, that what the delegates decide may rest on the Christian principles of justice and secure a true and lasting peace.

Leo XIII writes to the Archbishops and Bishops of Austria — of Vienna, Wroclaw, Prague, and Krakow — approving their long-pending plan to found a Catholic university. He expresses joy that the project, awaited under his predecessors, is nearing completion, urges the faithful to hasten it, and directs that its final arrangements be reported to the Sacred Congregation of Studies for approval under canonical norms.

John Paul II's first encyclical, opening his pontificate on the claim that Jesus Christ, the Redeemer of man, is the centre of the universe and of history. Taking up the inheritance of Vatican II, it turns to the man Redemption reaches — afraid of what his own progress has made, his rights honoured in letter or in spirit — and to the Church's answer in truth, in the Eucharist and Penance, and in service.

John Paul II's encyclical on the Blessed Virgin Mary in the life of the pilgrim Church, proclaiming a Marian Year before the third millennium. It follows Mary's pilgrimage of faith in three parts: her place in the mystery of Christ, from the Annunciation to “Behold your mother” at the Cross; her role at the center of the Church's journey toward Christian unity; and her maternal mediation, subordinate to Christ's one mediation.

Pius XI on the Catholic missions, setting two aims: more and better-trained missionaries, and lay Catholics who pray and give for them through the Society for the Propagation of the Faith. Its sharpest passage takes up Benedict XV's complaint that ancient mission territories still have no native bishops, and it commits the Pope to redividing and reassigning mission territories — to native clergy where possible — rather than leaving them to the institute that opened them.

es.text: Pío XI sobre las misiones católicas, con dos objetivos: más misioneros y mejor formados, y laicos que recen y contribuyan a ellos por medio de la Obra de la Propagación de la Fe. Su pasaje más incisivo retoma la queja de Benedicto XV de que territorios de misión antiguos siguen sin obispos autóctonos, y compromete al Papa a dividir y reasignar territorios de misión —al clero autóctono siempre que sea posible— en lugar de dejarlos al instituto que los abrió.

fr.text: Pie XI sur les missions catholiques, avec deux objectifs : davantage de missionnaires et mieux formés, et des laïcs qui prient et donnent pour eux par l'Œuvre de la Propagation de la Foi. Son passage le plus incisif reprend la plainte de Benoît XV selon laquelle d'anciens territoires de mission n'ont toujours pas d'évêques autochtones, et il engage le Pape à diviser et à réattribuer les territoires de mission — au clergé autochtone lorsque c'est possible — plutôt que de les laisser à l'institut qui les a ouverts.

it.text: Pio XI sulle missioni cattoliche, con due obiettivi: più missionari e meglio formati, e laici che preghino e contribuiscano per loro tramite l'Opera della Propagazione della Fede. Il passaggio più incisivo riprende la lamentela di Benedetto XV che territori di missione antichi siano ancora senza vescovi autoctoni, e impegna il Papa a dividere e riassegnare i territori di missione — al clero autoctono ove possibile — invece di lasciarli all'istituto che li ha aperti.

pt.text: Pio XI sobre as missões católicas, com dois objectivos: mais missionários e melhor formados, e leigos que rezem e contribuam para eles através da Obra da Propagação da Fé. A sua passagem mais incisiva retoma a queixa de Bento XV de que territórios de missão antigos continuam sem bispos autóctones, e compromete o Papa a dividir e reatribuir territórios de missão — ao clero autóctone sempre que possível — em vez de os deixar ao instituto que os abriu.

en.text: On the condition of labor amid industrial upheaval, addressing what the document itself calls the rights and duties of capital and labor. It refutes the socialist proposal to abolish private property, grounds ownership in natural and paternal right, sets out duties binding workers and employers alike, and turns to the roles of Church, State, and workingmen's associations in bettering the workman's condition.

pt.text: Encíclica de Leão XIII, de 1891, sobre a condição dos operários, escrita depois do fim das antigas corporações que os protegiam. Rejeita a solução socialista de abolir a propriedade particular como injusta, defende o direito natural à propriedade e à livre associação dos trabalhadores, e trata dos deveres do Estado, dos patrões e dos operários, incluindo a justa retribuição do trabalho.

en.text: Marks the third centenary of the death of St Francis de Sales, recounting his gentle but resolute holiness, surveying his major writings — the Introduction to the Devout Life, the Treatise on the Love of God, and the Controversies written during his mission to the Chablais — and declaring him heavenly patron of writers.

Pius XI's encyclical for the seventh centenary of the death of St. Francis of Assisi, describing him as God's providential answer to a medieval society riven by class hostility and moral decay. It surveys Francis's poverty, humility and obedience, the Rule he gave the Friars Minor, and the Second and Third Orders that grew from his reform, urging the world's bishops to promote the Third Order anew for the centenary.

Sacerdotalis Caelibatus, reaffirming the law of priestly celibacy in the Latin Church against the objections — doctrinal, historical, sociological, pastoral — raised after the Council, and grounding it in Christ's own celibacy and the priest's configuration to him. It treats the human dimensions of celibacy, formation in chastity, and dispensation for those who leave the priesthood, closing with an appeal to bishops and laity to sustain their priests.

Written for the centenary of the death of St John Mary Vianney, holding up the Curé of Ars as the model of a priest: his poverty, chastity and obedience, his life of prayer and his devotion to the Eucharist and the Mass, and his zeal as preacher, catechist and confessor. It closes by asking bishops, the faithful and the young themselves to foster priestly vocations.

Written to the bishops of Portugal for the eighth centenary of Portuguese independence, recalling how papal protection of the medieval kingdom bound its history to the spread of the faith through its missions. Pius XII asks for renewed recruitment and training of missionaries for the African and Asian territories, invokes Francis Xavier and John de Brito as patrons, and appeals to clergy and Catholic Action to sustain that work.

Leo XIII on the Church's three mission societies — the Propagation of the Faith, the Holy Infancy, and the Schools of the East — recounting the alms and prayers they gather for the missions, the growing shortage of missionaries at a time of persecution abroad and secularizing laws in Europe, and asking bishops, clergy and faithful to sustain the work with prayer, alms and vocations.

Written to the American hierarchy for the hundred-and-fiftieth anniversary of its establishment, recalling the growth of the Church in the United States from John Carroll's appointment as its first bishop to its present schools, missions and lay associations. It then warns against materialism in education and the breakdown of marriage, and asks for a just settlement of the labour question.

Settles the German 'trade union controversy': whether Catholic workers, alongside purely Catholic Arbeitervereine, may join mixed interconfessional labor unions with Protestants. Addressed to Cardinal Kopp and the German bishops, it reaffirms Rerum Novarum's principles and permits qualified toleration of the Christian Trade Unions where local conditions warrant, provided members also belong to a Catholic association and the unions never act against Church teaching, under episcopal oversight.

For the eleventh centenary of the death of St Methodius, presenting him with his brother Cyril as the apostles of the Slavs. It follows their lives and their peaceable missionary method — preaching and celebrating the liturgy in the language of the people they came to — and reads them as pioneers of what would later be called inculturation, who bound the Slav peoples into the Church's catholicity and into the common civilization of Christian Europe.

Benedict XVI on Christian hope, beginning from Paul's “in hope we were saved” and asking what kind of hope could make that true. It reads hope in the New Testament and the early Church, traces its modern replacement by faith in progress — from Bacon to the French and Marxist revolutions — and argues that progress builds no lasting kingdom. It then offers three settings in which hope is learned and practised: prayer, action and suffering, and judgement.

On St Jerome as the model and teacher of scriptural study, for the fifteenth centenary of his death: his life, his defence of the full divine inspiration and inerrancy of Scripture against those who would limit it, his rules for the literal and the spiritual senses, and his insistence that clergy, religious and laity alike read Scripture daily and find in it the person of Christ.

it.text: Per il sesto centenario della canonizzazione di san Tommaso d'Aquino: ne celebra la santità e la duplice sapienza, acquisita e infusa, proclamandolo Dottore Universale e Dottore Eucaristico. Ne addita la filosofia e la teologia come norma degli studi ecclesiastici, esorta i giovani a imitarne l'umiltà e la castità nella Milizia Angelica, e indice le celebrazioni centenarie con le relative indulgenze.

en.text: Pius XII's first encyclical, issued weeks into the Second World War, on the unity of the human family under Christ the King. It names two errors eroding that unity: forgetting mankind's common origin and equal dignity, and divorcing civil authority from God's law so that the State becomes its own supreme end. Written in what it calls an Hour of Darkness, it appeals for a return to unity through the Church.

Written to the bishops of Poland against the Mariavites, a society of self-styled Mystic Priests formed without episcopal permission around a woman its members held to be divinely inspired. Pius X confirms the 1904 decree suppressing it, refuses their professed submission as belied by their continued defiance of their bishops, and orders that those who persist in rebellion be dealt with severely.

Why the world has no true peace after the Great War: treaties that never reached the hearts of men, and a chronic war between the social classes. Against this Pius XI sets the peace of Christ, an effect of love rather than of justice alone; he calls the laity to disciplined cooperation with their bishops, condemns a moral, legal and social modernism, and closes protesting the unresolved Roman Question.

Pius X's protest against the 1905 French Law of Separation, addressed to the cardinals, bishops, clergy and people of France. It rejects separation of Church and state as “a thesis absolutely false” that denies God public worship and confines the state to this life alone, then itemises the law's injuries — the seizure of ecclesiastical property and pious foundations — before calling French Catholics to unity with their bishops and the Holy See.

es.text: Protesta de Pío X contra la Ley francesa de Separación de 1905, dirigida a los cardenales, obispos, clero y pueblo de Francia. Rechaza la separación entre la Iglesia y el Estado como «una tesis absolutamente falsa», que niega a Dios el culto público y confina al Estado a esta sola vida; enumera después los daños de la ley —la incautación de los bienes eclesiásticos y de las fundaciones pías— antes de llamar a los católicos franceses a la unión con sus obispos y con la Santa Sede.

fr.text: Protestation de Pie X contre la loi française de Séparation de 1905, adressée aux cardinaux, évêques, clergé et peuple de France. Elle rejette la séparation de l'Église et de l'État comme « une thèse absolument fausse », qui refuse à Dieu le culte public et enferme l'État dans cette seule vie ; elle énumère ensuite les atteintes de la loi — la saisie des biens ecclésiastiques et des fondations pieuses — avant d'appeler les catholiques français à l'union avec leurs évêques et avec le Saint-Siège.

it.text: Protesta di Pio X contro la legge francese di Separazione del 1905, indirizzata ai cardinali, ai vescovi, al clero e al popolo di Francia. Respinge la separazione tra Chiesa e Stato come «una tesi assolutamente falsa», che nega a Dio il culto pubblico e confina lo Stato a questa sola vita; enumera poi i danni della legge — la confisca dei beni ecclesiastici e delle fondazioni pie — prima di chiamare i cattolici francesi all'unione con i loro vescovi e con la Santa Sede.

pt.text: Protesto de Pio X contra a Lei francesa de Separação de 1905, dirigido aos cardeais, bispos, clero e povo de França. Rejeita a separação entre a Igreja e o Estado como «uma tese absolutamente falsa», que nega a Deus o culto público e confina o Estado a esta vida apenas; enumera depois os danos da lei — a apropriação dos bens eclesiásticos e das fundações pias — antes de chamar os católicos franceses à união com os seus bispos e com a Santa Sé.

en.text: John Paul II's encyclical to the bishops on the foundations of Catholic moral theology, written amid dissent from the Church's moral teaching. Framed by Christ's dialogue with the rich young man — “Teacher, what good must I do to have eternal life?” — it treats freedom's dependence on truth and God's law, conscience, the moral act, and intrinsically evil acts, closing with an appeal to Mary, Mother of Mercy.

Vatican II's decree on the pastoral office of bishops. It treats first their place in the college united with the pope — instituting the Synod of Bishops and calling for a reorganized Roman Curia — then the diocesan bishop's governance of his own particular church, in its boundaries, auxiliaries, curia, clergy and religious, and finally cooperation among bishops through episcopal conferences, ecclesiastical provinces, and inter-diocesan offices such as military vicariates.

The Second Vatican Council's dogmatic constitution on divine revelation. It describes revelation as God speaking to human beings as friends through deeds and words together, with Christ as both mediator and fullness; sets Scripture and Tradition as one deposit under the Church's teaching office; and holds that the inspired books teach without error the truth God wanted written for salvation. It closes by urging that all preaching, and the reading of all the faithful, be fed from Scripture.

pt.text: Constituição dogmática do Concílio Vaticano II sobre a Revelação divina: como Deus se revela e se comunica ao homem em Cristo, a sua transmissão pela sagrada Tradição e pela Sagrada Escritura sob a vigilância do Magistério, a inspiração e a verdade dos livros do Antigo e do Novo Testamento, e o lugar da Escritura na vida, no estudo e na leitura da Igreja.

en.text: Vatican II's declaration that the human person has a right to religious freedom: immunity from coercion, by individuals or government, in professing any religion, alone or in community. It argues the right rests first on human dignity and reason, then on revelation — since Christ invited faith rather than compelling it — and urges governments to secure it as a civil right within the bounds of just public order.

pt.text: Declaração do Concílio Vaticano II sobre a liberdade religiosa: afirma que a pessoa humana tem direito à liberdade religiosa, entendida como imunidade de coacção em matéria religiosa, em privado e em público, só ou associada a outros. Expõe primeiro a doutrina geral, fundada na dignidade da pessoa humana e na razão, e depois mostra-a radicada na Revelação divina e no comportamento de Cristo e dos Apóstolos.

en.text: The Church in the modern world, opening in solidarity with “the joys and the hopes, the griefs and the anxieties” of the age and addressed not only to the Church's own members but to the whole of humanity. Part I treats the dignity of the human person, human community, and human activity in the world; Part II takes up marriage and family, culture, economic and social life, the political community, and the fostering of peace among nations.

pt.text: Constituição pastoral do Vaticano II sobre a Igreja no mundo actual, que começa por fazer suas «as alegrias e as esperanças, as tristezas e as angústias» de toda a humanidade. A primeira parte trata a dignidade da pessoa humana, a comunidade humana e a actividade humana no mundo; a segunda, o matrimónio e a família, a cultura, a vida económico-social e política, e a promoção da paz entre as nações.

en.text: Vatican II's declaration on Christian education, opening from every person's inalienable right to an education suited to their nature and final end. It sets out parents as the first educators, the Church's own role in forming the baptized, and the purpose of Catholic schools, colleges, universities and faculties of sacred sciences, closing with a call for coordination among Catholic educational institutions.

pt.text: Declaração conciliar sobre a educação cristã, que parte do direito inalienável de todo o homem a uma educação correspondente à sua dignidade de pessoa. Afirma os pais como primeiros educadores, o papel próprio da Igreja na formação cristã dos baptizados, e a missão das escolas católicas, das universidades católicas e das faculdades de ciências sagradas, terminando com um apelo à coordenação entre as instituições escolares católicas.

en.text: The Council's decree on the media of social communications — press, cinema, radio, television. It claims the Church's right to use them and her duty to teach their right use, sets out the moral principles binding on those who make and those who consume them, including the claims of art and the protection of the young, and charges pastors, laity and a Roman office with a common apostolate.

The Council's dogmatic constitution on the Church: the mystery of the Church as sacrament and as People of God, then her hierarchical structure and the episcopate, the vocation of the laity, the universal call to holiness, the religious life, the pilgrim Church's bond with the Church in heaven, and last the place of Mary in the mystery of Christ and the Church.

pt.text: Constituição dogmática do Concílio Vaticano II sobre a Igreja, chamada luz dos povos e sacramento da união com Deus. Percorre o mistério da Igreja como povo de Deus e corpo de Cristo, sua constituição hierárquica de bispos, presbíteros e diáconos, a vocação dos leigos, o chamamento universal à santidade, a vida religiosa e a índole escatológica da Igreja peregrina, terminando com o lugar de Maria no mistério de Cristo e da Igreja.

en.text: Vatican II's declaration on the Church's relationship to non-Christian religions, moving from the questions common to all peoples about the meaning of existence through Hinduism and Buddhism, Islam, and above all Judaism, whose spiritual patrimony with Christianity it traces to Abraham and whose collective guilt for Christ's death it repudiates. It closes by rejecting all discrimination on grounds of race, color, condition, or religion.

Vatican II's decree on the training of future priests, requiring each episcopal conference to draft a national program adapting formation to local conditions. It treats the fostering of vocations, the organization of major seminaries, and a spiritual formation modeled on Christ the priest, then calls for ecclesiastical studies reorganized around the mystery of Christ with Scripture as theology's soul, adding pastoral training and formation continuing after ordination.

The Council's decree on the Eastern Catholic Churches — those in communion with Rome that follow the Byzantine, Alexandrian, Antiochene, Armenian or Chaldean rites rather than the Latin. It affirms their equal dignity with the Latin Church and their right to keep their own liturgical, disciplinary and spiritual patrimony, then treats patriarchal precedence, the discipline of the sacraments, worship and the calendar, and what common prayer with separated Eastern Christians is permitted.

The Council's constitution ordering a general restoration of the liturgy, directed at the full, conscious and active participation of the faithful. It lays down the principles of that reform and then works chapter by chapter through the Eucharist, the other sacraments and the sacramentals, the Divine Office, the liturgical year, sacred music and sacred art, admitting a wider use of the vernacular throughout.

pt.text: Estabelece os princípios gerais da reforma e do incremento da Liturgia, pedindo a participação plena, consciente e activa dos fiéis nas celebrações. Organiza-se em capítulos sobre a Eucaristia, os demais sacramentos e sacramentais, o Ofício Divino, o ano litúrgico, a música sacra, e a arte sacra e as alfaias litúrgicas, com um apêndice sobre a revisão do calendário.

en.text: The Council's decree on the restoration of unity among Christians, whose divisions it holds to be against Christ's will. It sets out the Catholic principles of ecumenism, including the elements of sanctification found in separated communities, treats its practice as rooted in interior conversion and dialogue, and considers separately the Eastern Churches and the communities separated from Rome in the West.
